To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found several new deeply embedded YSOs in AFGL 437, identified the driving source of the outflows and found the presence of a large diffuse neblousity associated with the central compact cluster and extending up 8.0 pc.

(i) the IRAC ratio map reveals the shocked H2 emission from the outflow associated with the deeply embedded massive YSO WK34; (ii) the IRAC images show that the diffuse nebulosity is associated with the central compact cluster and is likely to be caused by shocks from the compact cluster; and (iii) the SED modelling shows the YSOs within the central cluster to be massive and very young.
we have identified several new embedded young stars in the AFGL 437 star-forming region and we have studied the molecular outflows of the highly embedded YSOWK34 in the central compact cluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the massive cluster and the molecular outflows, and the identification of new embedded YSOs.
the physical properties of the embedded YSOs and their association with outflows and nebulosity in this star-forming region.
the physical nature of the embedded cluster and the surrounding diffuse nebulosity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the central cluster of AFGL 437 is a very active star-forming region with the presence of several young and deeply embedded massive protostars.
the central cluster of AFGL 437 is a massive young star cluster with a large number of YSOs in the range of intermediate to high-mass.
the massive star formation is ongoing in the central cluster of AFGL 437.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the massive cluster in AFGL 437 is still forming and the cluster is surrounded by an infrared bright nebulosity.
the central cluster is a massive cluster with a mass of ~200 M ⊙ and an age of ~5.0 × 10 5 yr.
the IRAC ratio maps provide a new tool to investigate the nature of the extended nebulosities around young clusters, which are not visible in the broad-band images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRAC data are useful in identifying new deeply embedded YSOs in a massive star-forming cloud and in studying the molecular outflows.
IRAC images can be used to identify embedded YSOs and their associated molecular outflows, and to investigate their physical properties.
the central cluster is a young and active cluster with several embedded YSOs, and the diffuse nebulosity is a consequence of the interaction of the cluster members.
